title: Spain Guardia Civil Recruitment 2026: Requirements Guide
metaDescription: Join the Guardia Civil in 2026: age limits, education, physical tests and the exam format for Spain's military police force, explained step by step.
headline: Spain Guardia Civil Recruitment 2026: How to Join

sections.title: Who can join the Guardia Civil?
sections.content:
The Guardia Civil is Spain's gendarmerie, a security force of a military nature that depends on both the Ministry of the Interior and the Ministry of Defence. The main entry route is the annual open competition for the Escala de Cabos y Guardias, the rank of corporal and guard. To apply you must hold Spanish nationality, be at least 18 years old and not have turned 40 in the year of the call.

The minimum education is the ESO school-leaving qualification or an equivalent, such as a basic vocational training diploma. You also need a valid category B driving licence, a clean record with no criminal convictions for intentional offences, and good civic conduct. Current rules set no general minimum height requirement, although the physical tests still demand a good level of fitness.

sections.title: The selection process and exam format
sections.content:
Selection combines a competitive examination phase with a merit assessment phase. The competitive phase starts with a knowledge test, a multiple-choice questionnaire of around 100 questions drawn from a syllabus of 25 topics, lasting about 90 minutes and requiring a minimum score to pass. Candidates also sit spelling and grammar tests, a foreign language test in English or French, and psychometric tests.

Those who pass the written stage face physical tests, with minimum standards that vary by sex and age, followed by a personal interview and a medical examination. Merit points are then added for qualifications, previous service and other achievements. The official call for each year, published in the BOE and on the Guardia Civil notice board, sets the exact dates, syllabus and scoring rules.

sections.title: Training at the academy
sections.content:
Successful candidates enter the Guardia Civil Academy, where training lasts about a year and combines classroom study with practical and physical instruction. Cadets study law, police procedure, weapons, first aid and driving, alongside military drill and sports, and they live on site under a disciplined routine.

On graduation, new guards are posted to a unit anywhere in Spain, from rural patrol posts to traffic, environmental or judicial police units. Further specialisation is possible later, including the rapid action group, the mountain rescue service and the canine unit, each with its own selection course and requirements.

sections.title: Pay and career prospects
sections.content:
Guardia Civil pay follows the public-sector scales for security forces, with a starting salary for a new guard that rises with seniority, rank and specialist allowances. Extra payments cover shift work, location and specific duties, and the force provides a pension and job security that make it one of the most sought-after public careers in Spain.

Promotion runs from Guardia to Cabo, Sargento and beyond, through internal competitions and courses. Many guards also use their service to move into specialist units or to apply for officer training later. For candidates who want a stable uniformed career with a strong sense of public service, the annual call is the gateway.

faqs.q: What is the age limit for the Guardia Civil?
faqs.a: You must be at least 18 years old and must not have turned 40 in the year of the call, so applicants up to 39 can normally apply. The exact limit is confirmed in each year's official call, published in the BOE, and it applies to the year of the competition rather than the day you apply. Separate officer routes set their own age limits.

faqs.q: What education do I need for the Guardia Civil?
faqs.a: The minimum qualification is the ESO school-leaving certificate or an equivalent recognised in Spain, such as a basic or intermediate vocational training diploma. Some candidates also qualify through university access routes for over-25s. A category B driving licence is required, and any qualification must be held or obtainable before the first test, as stated in the call.

faqs.q: Is there a minimum height for the Guardia Civil?
faqs.a: Current regulations set no general minimum height requirement for the Guardia Civil, although older rules once required 1.65 metres for men and 1.60 metres for women. The physical tests still apply demanding minimum standards for running, strength and agility, with different thresholds by sex and age, so fitness preparation matters far more than height today.

faqs.q: How hard is the Guardia Civil exam?
faqs.a: The knowledge test is the main filter: around 100 multiple-choice questions from a 25-topic syllabus in about 90 minutes, with a minimum pass mark. Candidates must also pass spelling, psychometric and physical tests, an interview and a medical. Thousands apply for each annual call, so steady study of the syllabus and regular fitness training are essential.
